reasoning_quality_informational.v1_root_problem: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul) to 1180-1260/month in Aug-Sep 2026 (E-07/F-06). A field-reader staffing shortfall since July (E-06) is linked to manual-read route completion falling to 0.88 against a 0.95 target across 9,200 accounts (E-01/F-01), which increases estimate-substituted billing and drives part of the surge, but this mechanism explains at most a minority of disputed bills since 59% (1785/3025) were on ACTUAL, not estimated, reads (E-02/F-02/F-03) — leaving a second, not-yet-established mechanism behind most of the surge.
reasoning_quality_informational.v2_root_problem: Billing dispute tickets rose from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to 1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-07) because billing-import validation rule BV-17 -- a high-consumption check with no unit scaling, deployed 2026-08-01 exactly as the surge began (E-12) -- rejects otherwise-valid, timely AMI reads as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION and forces estimate substitution, accounting for 1184 of the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills (95.5%, E-11). Whether this same unscaled rule also drives the larger 59% ACTUAL-read dispute segment remains unconfirmed (H-BV17-UNIT-SCALING-ACTUAL, candidate only).
reasoning_quality_informational.ideal_final_problem: BV-17 validation rejects valid firmware-v4.2 AMI reads (unit-scale mismatch on H-MDMS-BILL) and substitutes estimates.
